s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent skin fragility with seasonal variation and superficial erosions
salient_findings: Superficial skin erosions with linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
key_facts: 2-year-old girl presented with skin fragility
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Physical and mental developments were normal
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
Hair, nails, and mucous membranes were normal
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Skin biopsy showed complete separation of the stratum corneum
Genetic study revealed 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene

shortlist.label: Peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of skin fragility, superficial erosions, and seasonal variation match this condition

shortlist.label: Acral peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction and seasonal variation are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: CDSN-related peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic study revealed 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene, which is associated with this condition

shortlist.label: Samira type peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical features such as mild xerosis, superficial skin erosions, and erythematous residual macules are similar to this condition

shortlist.label: Generalized peeling skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Widespread skin involvement and superficial erosions are consistent with this diagnosis
